messages:
Nina Park: Noticed the API ref for PATCH /v1/models/{model_id}/settings has incorrect enum and example details. The YAML lists visibility: [public, private] but the service accepts an additional 'org' value and default is 'private' (doc currently says public). I opened a PR to fix the OpenAPI schema, examples, and SDK snippets: https://git.redwood/infra/docs/pulls/4720
Ethan Li: Oof, that explains some confusion from customers. Can you paste the corrected request example and a Go client snippet? I'll update the docs site after merge.
Nina Park: Sure — preferred canonical example and note:

curl -X PATCH "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/mdl_123/settings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"visibility":"org","max_sequence_length":4096}'

// Go (net/http)
reqBody := `{"visibility":"org","max_sequence_length":4096}`
req, _ := http.NewRequest("PATCH", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/mdl_123/settings", strings.NewReader(reqBody))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
resp, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
// handle resp

Callout: visibility enum now: [private, public, org]. Default is private (not public). Also response now returns updated_at and settings_revision — add both to response examples.
Ravi Desai: Good catch. I'll update the OpenAPI YAML: add enum entry, set default: private, and extend response schema with updated_at and settings_revision (string + integer). Also sweep the Node/Python snippets for wording.
docs-bot: PR 4720 created and linted: https://git.redwood/infra/docs/pulls/4720 :white_check_mark:
Ethan Li: I'll review and run the preview build. If the staging render looks good, can we include a short migration note: older clients assumed default public and may have unintentionally exposed models. Suggest adding a short security note and recommending explicit visibility in client code.
Nina Park: Added a one-line security blurb to the PR description. Thanks — will mark resolved after merge. :lock:
